reasoning: The two sets are nearly identical: same brief, spec, stage split, ten-milestone roadmap, reference summaries with correct caveats (RF-01's whole-sample PCA becomes a per-window fit in AD-16/AD-20), null-hypothesis-testing and data-analysis routing, and the same 46-task M1 plan. The differences all favour A. B swaps the live-progress channel the user asked for (WebSocket) for Server-Sent Events, and its AD-07 even rejects WebSockets as unnecessary. That runs through B's architecture, contracts, pipelines and the M1-T23, M1-T34 and M1-T40 packets. A keeps the WebSocket at `/runs/{id}/ws` with seq resume throughout. A gives every designed milestone checkable Exit criteria; B has Exit criteria only on M1 and also leaves out frontend-design on M2, which builds explorer pages. A adds qdata golden cases (split day, dividend day, effective-date membership, a late dividend, a reused ticker, first-known stamping) for M1's core point-in-time logic, while B has none. A orders the interface tasks correctly (qserver depends on qdata, explorer on qserver); B runs all three at once and has to add a risk line admitting the import checks fail until M1-T01 merges. A's Covers lines agree with its Deferred list; B's M1-T04/T05 claim DATA-01 and M1-T18 claims CHECK-09, both of which its own Scope defers. A drops the stale spec open question that B keeps. B's M1-T20/M1-T40 acceptance ('every route in api.create_app answers') contradicts mount_studies being deferred to M5; A spells out the M1 route subset. A still has a few faults: its M8 test range takes in PL-40 cases while PL-40 is listed under M9; it says 'the brief asks for a WebSocket' when the brief doesn't; and both sets point Sharadar at Nasdaq Data Link rather than api.sharadar.com.
